page.title: How to build a scalable React app with Next.js and TypeScript
page.description: A practical foundation for building maintainable, type-safe React apps with Next.js and TypeScript.

text.content: Getting a Next.js app running with TypeScript is easy.

rich_text.plain_text: Getting a Next.js app running with TypeScript is easy.

text.content: Keeping it pleasant to work in after six months of product changes is the harder part.

rich_text.plain_text: Keeping it pleasant to work in after six months of product changes is the harder part.

text.content: That’s where a lot of React apps start to creak. Not because React is bad, or Next.js is bad, or someone picked the wrong folder structure on day one. Usually it happens slowly. A page starts doing too much. A shared component gets one too many business rules. A hook becomes the secret home for fetching, formatting, permissions, and modal state. Suddenly every “small change” feels a little risky.
